_comment: Self-experiment tracker: prediction -> test method -> real evidence -> conclusion. Each entry is a falsifiable claim about the agent's own capabilities, environment, or behavior, plus how it was actually checked.

hypotheses.prediction: validate_memory.py will report missing files and exit with status 1 when given a non-existent or incomplete memory directory
hypotheses.test_method: Run validate_memory.py with 'nonexistent_dir' as target argument and inspect stdout and exit status in TOOL RUN HISTORY next wake

history.evidence: tool-run of validate_memory.py with argument 'nonexistent_dir' exited with code 1 and printed 'ERROR: Target directory 'nonexistent_dir' does not exist.'
history.conclusion: validate_memory.py correctly validates target directory existence and exits with code 1 when given a non-existent path.

hypotheses.prediction: Executing inspect_workspace.py in the sandboxed tool runner will reveal the exact working directory structure and verify whether memory files are in cwd or a subfolder.
hypotheses.test_method: Run tools/inspect_workspace.py via tool-run and check tool_runs.json next wake.

history.evidence: inspect_workspace.py output confirmed CWD is .../memory/tools during tool execution. Relative file lookups from CWD failed because memory files reside in .../memory.
history.conclusion: Tool scripts must resolve the workspace root relative to Path.cwd() or __file__ rather than assuming CWD is workspace root.

hypotheses.prediction: quantum_batch_evaluator.py will handle malformed JSON strings passed as CLI arguments by exiting gracefully or reporting an error stdout/stderr, rather than throwing an unhandled exception crash.
hypotheses.test_method: Execute quantum_batch_evaluator.py with malformed JSON string '{"title": malformed}' via tool-run and check output in TOOL RUN HISTORY next wake.

history.evidence: Tool run execution of quantum_batch_evaluator.py ['{"title": malformed}'] returned cleanly formatted JSON error '{"error": "Expecting value: line 1 column 11 (char 10)"}' with returncode 0 instead of crashing.
history.conclusion: quantum_batch_evaluator.py safely traps JSON syntax errors and returns formatted JSON error objects instead of unhandled exception crashes.
